title: Draft
description: Something this project is about to say outside itself, while it can still be changed.
guidance: The body is the post, exactly as it would be read by somebody who has never seen this project — no headings, no internal names, no record keys. Say what changed and why it matters to them; a changelog entry is not a post. Set `channel` before anything else: it is the key of a `posts.channel` record, and through it comes the account this goes out as, how long the post may be and what `visibility` may say. A draft with no channel has nowhere to go. Link the records it was assembled from with `assembled_from`, so whoever reads it later can check the claim rather than believe it.

channel.description: The key of the `posts.channel` record this is written for — an account, not a network. A key rather than the name of a service, because two projects on one machine publish to one network under different accounts, and because a draft has to keep pointing at the right one when a second is added. Absent means nobody has decided yet, which is an ordinary state for a draft and the one state it cannot be sent in.

visibility.description: Who would be able to read it, in the vocabulary of its channel's own network — LinkedIn has two values, and the other three give an ordinary account none. A string rather than an enum for exactly that reason: one shared set would offer a value the chosen network has never heard of. What is valid is checked against the network by the section that writes it.

assembled_from.description: The records this was written out of — the decision it announces, the observation behind it. What makes a claim in a post checkable rather than remembered.
